H1.name: risk-state switch: equal-weight sectors <-> defensive trio
H1.rule: At each session close t: if T(t) = 1 (risk-off) hold the equal-weight defensive leg; else hold the equal-weight risk-on leg. Execute at the close of t+1 when the state changes; also rebalance to the current leg's equal weights at each month-end. Fully invested in equities; never cash.

riskon_leg.D_H: equal weight of all eligible sector SPDRs
riskon_leg.L: equal weight of the 12 French industries

reasons_from_D_only: Risk-on leg = equal-weight sectors: on D no sector-selection rule beat equal weight (J2* = B5; Q1 point estimates -1.6 to -3.4 pp/yr; B6/B7 momentum also below B5), and equal weight is the neutral, unselected choice. SPY was rejected because it adds a cap-weight bet the defensive leg does not share; a declared high-beta set was rejected because choosing it would use D outcomes (a forking path).

Defensive leg = XLP/XLU/XLV: from peak to trough the trio beat SPY in every D episode (+31.5, +19.2, +12.9, +9.6, +10.7 pp in 2000-02, 2008-09, 2011, 2015-16, 2018Q4; results_stage_D.json episode_holdings_D).
Switch tied to T, not sector momentum: on D the sector RS rules did not reach the defensives before the peak in 2000 or 2007 (episode holdings), so momentum is the wrong trigger for this switch.

T rather than J1-E (crisis-only): J1-E exited before the trough in only 2 of 6 D episodes and stayed fully invested through 1998, 2011, 2015-16 and 2018Q4 - the four episodes where the trio still beat SPY by 9.6-12.9 pp. A recession-confirmed trigger cannot capture those.

Faster trigger is acceptable here because the fallback is defensives, not cash: on D, T's false risk-off spells cost 3.73%/calm-yr against SPY when the fallback was cash (B3, 2.85 false pivots/calm-yr). With a defensive fallback the cost of a false spell is the equal-weight-minus-trio spread, not the equity premium minus bills; the trio has beta about 0.6 (atlas, census) so a false spell keeps most of an up-move. That asymmetry is the argument for T over J1-E.

T rather than T-and-credit (J1-B): on D J1-B and B3 exited on near-identical dates in all six episodes (pivot table), credit reduced false pivots (1.74 vs 2.85/calm-yr) but the lower false-pivot cost under a defensive fallback reduces that benefit, and credit is not available across L (repo DBAA from 1986 only), which would make H1 H-only. T keeps H1 testable on ~70 years.

No H1 D outcome was computed or seen. To size the power line the H1 book was simulated on D and only the bootstrap standard error of the contrast was printed (script /home/ubuntu2/tmp/rotation-core/v2/power_h1_D.py); the point estimate was deliberately not printed.
H1.primary_contrast: annualised mean daily return of H1 minus its exposure-matched static mix X1 = w_on x (risk-on leg) + (1 - w_on) x (defensive leg), daily rebalanced, costless, where w_on = fraction of sessions H1 held the risk-on leg on the window tested (rebuilt per sample and per era)
H1.L_clean: PARTLY. Clean at industry level: no industry-panel return of any kind has been computed. Not clean for the signal: the risk-state series T and its market-level timing against cash on 1928-1997 were seen in the v1 Stage D long tier (B3). What is unseen is how the trio performed against the equal-weight industries inside T's states.

power_from_D_variance_only.assumption: SE scaled by sqrt(n_D / n); assumes per-session contrast variance equal to D's (optimistic for L, whose 1929-1940s volatility was higher)

H2.name: crisis de-risk: exit to cash only when recession confirmation and the trend trigger agree
H2.rule: Identical to v1 J1-E: SPY weight 0 if (T and M) else 1; daily rule, trades only on change; remainder in cash.
H2.why_unchanged: J1-E was the best J1 candidate on D (P1 +2.96%, raw p 0.06; G2, G3 and all G6 risk tests except exit-before-trough met). Changing its earlier trigger after seeing D (for example to credit) would be a new rule chosen on D - a forking path. It is carried unchanged so that D-selection is the only contamination.
H2.primary_contrast: annualised mean daily return of H2 minus X2 = w x SPY + (1 - w) x cash, w = mean H2 SPY weight on the window tested
H2.L_clean: NO. J1-E's market-level performance on 1960-1997 was computed in the v1 Stage D long tier, and M (real-time Sahm) does not exist before 1959-12, with no substitute that is both real-time and long. H2 is H-only.

power_from_D_variance_only.statement: H2 cannot detect any plausible effect on H; its realistic outcome is L0 whatever happens.

third_hypothesis.considered: J3-C (risk-state cross-asset rotation) vs its primary comparator R1 (exposure-matched equal-weight 7 sleeves)
third_hypothesis.why_left_out: On D its primary contrast R1 was +3.33% with raw p 0.13 (Holm 0.63); the only strong number was the secondary R2 vs GTAA, and promoting the secondary would be selection on D. It has no L sample (cross-asset ETFs start 2002-2007; the J3 proxy tier would rest on J1-B's credit flag, which is not available before 1997), so it would be H-only with a minimum detectable effect of about 11 pp/yr. Adding it would raise Holm m to 3 and cost power for H1 without a realistic chance of a result.

decision_rule.why_pooled_plus_sign: H alone cannot detect less than about 4.7 pp/yr for H1, so requiring separate significance on H would make the test a formality. Pooling L and H uses all unseen industry-level evidence; requiring the H point estimate to be positive guards against an effect that existed only before 1998. L is required positive too, so neither sample can carry the result alone.

L1_accepted_historical.H1: all of: Holm p < 0.05 on the pooled contrast; pooled estimate >= +1.0 pp/yr; L estimate > 0 and H estimate > 0; pooled Holm p < 0.05 and estimate >= +1.0 pp/yr at 2x costs; pooled stress-episode capture vs SPY <= 0.80 (L and H episodes combined); CAGR >= risk-on leg CAGR - 1.0 pp/yr on L and on H.
L1_accepted_historical.H2: all of: Holm p < 0.05 on H; H estimate >= +1.0 pp/yr; holds at 2x costs; max drawdown <= 0.70 x SPY max drawdown on H; CAGR >= SPY - 2.0 pp/yr on H.
